Director Non-Sterile Operations
Thermo Fisher Scientific
Greenville, NC
Work Schedule
Standard (Mon-Fri)
Environmental Conditions
Adherence to all Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) Safety Standards
As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.
Location/Division Specific Information
As part of the Drug Product Division (DPD), the Greenville, North Carolina site is a multi-purpose pharmaceutical development, manufacturing, and packaging campus. The operation specializes in taking both sterile injectable and oral solid dose drug products from development phase through to commercialization.
Position Summary
The Director, Non-Sterile Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for non-sterile manufacturing operations, with primary accountability for packaging, inspection, and device assembly, including Auto Injector Assembly. The role also oversees Oral Solid Dose (OSD) and Continuous Manufacturing (CM) platforms as part of the site’s non-sterile portfolio.
This position ensures the safe, compliant, and efficient execution of manufacturing and packaging activities from development through commercialization. The Director drives operational excellence and continuous improvement while partnering cross-functionally to deliver performance across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and people in alignment with evolving site priorities and growth platforms.
Key Responsibilities
Lead and oversee non-sterile operations with primary focus on primary and secondary packaging, inspection, and Auto Injector Assembly, while maintaining operational excellence across OSD and Continuous Manufacturing platforms.
Own operational performance across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and people, driving accountability and measurable results.
Strengthen packaging, inspection, device assembly, OSD, and CM capabilities through operational rigor, process robustness, and appropriate technology enablement.
Ensure sustained cGMP compliance through strong quality systems, documentation practices, investigations, CAPA, and risk management.
Support technology transfer, scale-up, and commercialization activities across packaging, device assembly, OSD, and CM programs.
Develop high-performing teams and foster a culture of engagement, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Management, or related field (or equivalent experience).
10+ years of progressive operations leadership experience in pharmaceutical or biopharmaceutical manufacturing, including sterile manufacturing in a regulated environment.
Demonstrated experience in a cGMP-regulated environment, including strong understanding of regulations governing sterile injectable packaging, combination products, and medical device manufacturing (e.g., FDA 21 CFR Parts 210/211, 820, EU GMP, and applicable ISO standards).
Experience with automated assembly systems, high-speed packaging lines, continuous manufacturing technologies, and continuous improvement methodologies preferred.
Strong leadership, financial, and strategic acumen with the ability to influence stakeholders and build high-performing teams.
Ability to travel up to 25% including international locations.

Vice President Operations
Alec's Ice Cream
El Segundo, CA
About Alec’s Ice Cream
Alec’s Ice Cream is building a next-generation food company focused on naturally better-for-you daily indulgences. We believe consumers should not have to choose between exceptional taste, ingredient integrity, and products they can feel good about enjoying regularly.
We are changing the way people indulge by creating products that feel more modern, more craveable, and more aligned with what consumers want today. Our goal is to help redefine the category and build the brand that becomes the defining next-generation name in ice cream.
For people who want to be self-starters, own their function with real autonomy, and work with a values-led team on a big mission, Alec’s is a place to do meaningful work and help build something exceptional.
Role Description
The Vice President of Operations is a full-time, hybrid role based in El Segundo, CA. VP of Operations owns the end-to-end supply chain, from raw material purchasing and co-packer management through order fulfillment.
The VP of Operations reports directly to the CEO and leads both the supply chain organization and manufacturing partners, including Quality Assurance. As a key member of the leadership team, this executive will have broad influence across manufacturing, supply planning, warehousing and distribution, capacity, continuous improvement, and operational performance. This is an opportunity to build a strong foundation, develop high-performing teams, and create scalable solutions that support continued growth.
Key Responsibilities
Co-Packer & Production Oversight
Own the relationship with our co-packing partners, who are critical to the business: run regular business reviews, set clear performance expectations, and resolve issues at the executive level
Ensure production capacity is always available to meet demand by partnering with co-packers on capacity planning, scheduling, and forward commitments ahead of forecasted growth
Build redundancy into the network by qualifying and onboarding backup or secondary co-packers to protect against capacity shortfalls or quality failures
Lead contract negotiations and cost discussions as agreements come up for renewal or as new co-packers are added
Monitor production yields and performance, troubleshoot issues that affect cost, quality, or service, and drive co-packer cost reductions and efficiency gains
Strategic Sourcing & Procurement
Develop and implement sourcing strategy for raw materials and packaging
Negotiate strategic supplier agreements and pricing; manage overall vendor performance
Onboard and qualify new suppliers to optimize sourcing strategy and reduce overall input costs
Inventory & Demand Planning
Translate demand forecasts into production and inventory plans with co-packers and raw material suppliers
Plan raw material and packaging requirements, capacity, and shelf life to keep inventory at target levels
Set safety stock levels and manage inventory to minimize waste and obsolescence
Order Fulfillment & Logistics
Oversee frozen warehousing, 3PL partners, and freight across the network, run regular business reviews, and maintain cold-chain integrity from plant to customer
Own on-time-in-full (OTIF) performance against retailer and distributor requirements, track and report root causes of misses, reduce chargebacks and fines, and put corrective actions in place to prevent repeat issues
Manage logistics spend and carrier relationships, run freight bids, and drive load consolidation
Quality Assurance
Ensure product meets spec and food safety standards across all production runs
Own audit readiness and compliance documentation
Ensure product consistency and adherence to sensory specifications across all production runs and co-packers
Develop and maintain a comprehensive quality manual and a formal co-packer quality management process, including audits, corrective actions, and spec sign-off
Team Leadership
Build, lead, and scale a high-performing supply chain and manufacturing organization, including QA, by hiring and developing talent and defining clear roles and responsibilities
Set clear goals and performance expectations, provide regular coaching and feedback, and invest in the growth of direct reports
Qualifications & Experience
10+ years in food/CPG supply chain and manufacturing operations, with end-to-end experience across planning, sourcing, and logistics, and direct experience managing a large team
Hands-on experience with inventory management, demand forecasting, and ERP/supply chain planning systems
Experience building or scaling a QA function
Strong analytical skills; comfortable owning and reporting on COGS-driving metrics
Excellent negotiation and vendor management skills
Experience managing new product commercialization or launch processes in a food/CPG environment
P&L or margin ownership experience, with a track record of delivering measurable cost reductions
Food safety knowledge preferred (SQF/BRC/HACCP exposure a plus); certification not required
Ability and willingness to travel for co-packer and vendor site visits

Fashion meets innovation in the design of our two state-of-the-art facilities based in the heart of Austin, Texas, and overflows into the design of our growing retail environment across the country.

capture.text:
Plant Manager
Gutchess Lumber Co., Inc.
Freedom, NY
No longer accepting applications
Position Summary
Job title: Plant Manager
Company: Gutchess Lumber Co., Inc.
Location: Freedom, NY sawmill
Reports to: Larry Lines, VP of Operations
FLSA status: Exempt, salaried
Schedule: Full time; presence across shifts, with weekend and on-call coverage as operations require
Travel: Occasional, to Cortland and other Gutchess facilities
About the Role
Gutchess Lumber Co., Inc. is a family-owned hardwood producer headquartered in Cortland, NY, sawing and kiln-drying Appalachian and Northern hardwoods for domestic and export customers.
The Plant Manager leads the Freedom sawmill from log intake through sawing, grading, and shipping. The role sets the safety culture, hits production and recovery targets, and develops the crew. It works closely with log procurement, sales, kiln operations, and corporate finance.
Key Responsibilities
Safety and Environmental
Own the site safety program: lockout/tagout, machine guarding, mobile equipment, PPE, hearing conservation, combustible dust and fire prevention.
Lead incident investigation, root-cause analysis, and corrective action; ensure OSHA 300 logs and training records are maintained and current.
Maintain compliance with NYSDEC air, stormwater and solid-waste permits and any other site permits.
Production and Recovery
Plan and schedule daily and weekly production to meet volume, species, grade and thickness targets set with Sales.
Drive lumber recovery and yield from log to board; track uptime, throughput and downtime direct causes and resolve.
Coordinate log deck inventory and log flow with procurement; manage green lumber flow to kilns or shipping.
Oversee residuals (chips, sawdust, bark) handling and sales logistics.
Quality and Grading
Ensure lumber meets NHLA grading rules and customer specifications, including thickness, sawing accuracy, and end-trim.
Support grader training and certification; resolve customer quality claims with Sales.
Maintenance and Capital
Direct preventive and predictive maintenance for headrig, resaw, edger, trimmer, debarker, conveyors, and rolling stock.
Manage saw filing and tooling programs.
Identify, justify, and manage capital projects and equipment upgrades.
People and Leadership
Hire, train, schedule, coach and evaluate supervisors and hourly staff; build bench strength and cross-training.
Apply company policies fairly and consistently, partnering with HR on employee relations and discipline.
Communicate goals and results to the crew and promote a culture of safety, accountability and continuous improvement.
Work collaboratively with HR and plant leadership.
Cost and Reporting
Prepare and manage the plant operating budget; control labor, maintenance, supplies and energy costs.
Report production, safety, quality and cost KPIs to leadership using company systems (e.g. Epicor and plant reports).
Maintain accurate tallies, inventory and production records, including chain-of-custody and log origin documentation where required (e.g. EUDR).
Qualifications
Required
Experience of manufacturing management experience, including leading a sawmill or wood products operation.
Working knowledge of hardwood sawmill equipment, log scaling and NHLA grading rules.
Proven record improving safety performance, recovery, and uptime.
Experience building budgets, controlling costs, and reporting KPIs.
Proficiency with ERP systems and Microsoft Office, especially Excel.
Valid driver’s license.
Preferred
Bachelor’s degree in forestry, wood science, engineering, business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
NHLA Inspector Training School completion or grading experience.
Lean, Six Sigma, or similar continuous improvement training.
OSHA 30-hour General Industry certification.
Experience with sawmill optimization or scanning systems and export-grade lumber.
Experience using AI tools to improve productivity, analysis, and decision-making.
Core Competencies
Safety leadership: stops unsafe work and models safe behavior every day.
Hands-on problem solving: diagnoses equipment and process issues on the floor.
People development: coaches supervisors and grows talent from within.
Business acumen: connects log mix, recovery and grade outcomes to plant profitability.
Communication: works clearly with crews, peers and leadership.
Integrity: keeps records accurate and confidential information protected.
Physical Demands and Work Environment
The role splits time between the office and the mill floor, log yard, and lumber yard. Reasonable accommodations will be made for qualified individuals with disabilities.
Walk, stand, climb stairs and catwalks, and work around moving machinery for extended periods.
Lift up to 50 lb occasionally.
Work in noise, dust, vibration, and outdoor conditions, including Western New York winters.
Wear required PPE, including hearing, eye, head, and foot protection.
Compensation and Benefits
Benefits: Medical, dental, vision, 401(k), ESOP, life insurance, short-term/long-term disability, accident insurance.
Time off: Paid time off, paid holidays.
Equal Opportunity Employer
Gutchess Lumber Co., Inc. is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Global Head of Enterprise Standards
Analog Devices
Austin, TX
About Analog Devices
Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X.
Global Head of Enterprise Standards
The Opportunity
Analog Devices is seeking a Global Head of Enterprise Standards to provide executive leadership for software quality, functional safety, product security assurance, and Responsible AI governance across products, software, systems, and emerging technologies. This role will shape the strategies, operating models, capabilities, and assurance practices that enable ADI to deliver safe, secure, reliable, and trustworthy products while accelerating responsible innovation.
As the enterprise leader for these four critical disciplines, you will partner with executive leadership, engineering organizations, product groups, Legal, Regulatory Affairs, and business teams to embed quality, safety, security, and responsible AI throughout the product and technology lifecycle. A core part of Responsible AI governance will be establishing effective data governance for AI, recognizing that trustworthy outcomes depend on the quality, provenance, ownership, protection, permitted use, and ongoing stewardship of the data used to train, validate, deploy, and monitor AI systems. Standards engagement, certification readiness, regulatory coordination, and governance frameworks will serve as key enablers of this mission, strengthening customer trust, managing enterprise risk, and supporting ADI’s technology leadership.
Responsibilities
Quality, Safety, Security, and Responsible AI
Set the global strategy and operating model for software quality, functional safety, product security assurance, and Responsible AI governance.
Lead and develop global teams of technical leaders and subject-matter experts across these four disciplines.
Drive software development quality and process maturity through risk-based assurance, lifecycle governance, measurement, independent oversight, and continuous improvement.
Establish functional safety capabilities that integrate hazard analysis, safety planning, safety cases, assessment, and assurance into product and system development.
Direct product security assurance across secure development lifecycles, security risk assessment, vulnerability management, product incident readiness, and independent assurance.
Lead Responsible AI governance, including integrated AI and data governance, use-case risk classification, lifecycle controls, human oversight, evaluation, monitoring, and accountability.
Establish data governance as a foundational element of AI governance, with clear accountability for data ownership and stewardship, data quality and fitness for purpose, provenance and lineage, access and usage rights, privacy and security, retention, third-party data, documentation, and controls for training, validation, deployment, and monitoring data.
Partner with enterprise data, privacy, security, legal, and engineering leaders to ensure AI data practices are consistent, traceable, risk-based, and aligned with business objectives and responsible-use commitments.
Ensure development processes support safe, secure, reliable, high-quality, and trustworthy products and solutions.
Define performance measures and assurance reporting that provide executive visibility into maturity, risk, product readiness, and business outcomes.
Enable responsible innovation at scale by embedding proportionate quality, safety, security, and AI governance practices early in the product and technology lifecycle.
Standards, Certification, and Regulatory Enablement
Use relevant standards, regulatory requirements, and certification programs to strengthen software quality, functional safety, product security, and Responsible AI capabilities.
Lead the ADI Standards Office and focus external engagement on standards that materially support product assurance, innovation, customer needs, and market access.
Monitor emerging requirements, assess their implications for the four core disciplines, and sponsor timely readiness plans.
Coordinate enterprise product regulatory activities for CE marking, including applicable EU requirements, conformity-assessment planning, technical documentation, testing and certification evidence, EU Declarations of Conformity, and cross-functional market-readiness decisions.
Oversee certification readiness and continuous improvement where certification provides strategic, customer, regulatory, or operational value.
External Engagement and Industry Influence
Represent ADI in selected standards organizations, industry consortia, certification organizations, and regulatory forums relevant to software quality, functional safety, product security, and Responsible AI.
Build strategic relationships with customers, regulators, certification partners, standards bodies, and industry peers.
Influence future industry practices and benchmarks in areas important to ADI’s products, technologies, and customers.
Position ADI as a recognized leader in safe, secure, high-quality, and trustworthy technology development.
Organizational Leadership and Business Impact
Lead global, multidisciplinary teams and subject-matter experts across software quality, functional safety, product security assurance, Responsible AI, and supporting standards activities.
Set organizational direction, deploy resources, develop talent, and build succession plans for critical technical and governance capabilities.
Drive alignment among business units, engineering organizations, and corporate functions on risk-based product assurance priorities.
Advise and mentor technical and business leaders on quality, safety, security, trustworthy AI, and responsible innovation.
Establish measures for process maturity, product readiness, risk reduction, assurance effectiveness, audit and certification outcomes, and business value.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, computer science, software engineering, quality, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Extensive leadership experience in the semiconductor, technology, software, embedded systems, or a related industry.
Demonstrated executive expertise in multiple core areas among software quality, functional safety, product security assurance, and Responsible AI governance, with the ability to integrate them into an enterprise operating model.
Proven experience building and leading global technical organizations and influencing complex, cross-functional stakeholder groups.
Strong understanding of product and software development lifecycles, risk-based assurance, independent assessment, governance, and continuous improvement.
Demonstrated success improving organizational maturity and embedding quality, safety, security, or trustworthy AI practices into engineering execution.
Exceptional executive communication, influencing, collaboration, and stakeholder-management skills.
Preferred Qualifications
Advanced degree in engineering, computer science, technology, business, or a related discipline.
Experience leading enterprise software quality or software process improvement programs, including assurance, metrics, corrective action, and lifecycle governance.
Experience with functional safety engineering and assurance for safety-related products or systems.

Experience establishing integrated Responsible AI and data governance frameworks, including data ownership and stewardship, quality and fitness for purpose, provenance and lineage, access controls, privacy, security, documentation, and lifecycle oversight for AI-enabled systems.

Experience representing a company in selected certification bodies, consortia, regulatory forums, or standards development organizations.
Why You Will Like Working at ADI
At Analog Devices, you will shape how software quality, functional safety, product security assurance, and Responsible AI are built into breakthrough innovation across the intelligent edge. You will lead global experts, strengthen product and engineering capabilities, and create the trusted foundation that allows ADI and its customers to move ahead of what’s possible.

Director of Quality Assurance and Risk Management
The Sanctuary | Cullman, Alabama
Job Type: Full-Time
Schedule: Monday through Friday, with weekends and after-hours as organizational needs require.
Reports To: Chief Executive Officer / Director of Nursing
About The Sanctuary
The Sanctuary is a 40-bed inpatient psychiatric hospital expanding to 46 beds, providing compassionate behavioral health services to adult and geriatric patients.
We are seeking an experienced, detail-oriented, and proactive Director of Quality Assurance and Risk Management to join our leadership team. This individual will play a critical role in promoting patient safety, maintaining regulatory compliance, strengthening clinical quality, and driving continuous organizational improvement.
Position Overview
The Director is responsible for overseeing the facility's Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement (QAPI), Risk Management, Patient Safety, and Regulatory Compliance programs.
The ideal candidate is a hands-on leader who can identify organizational risks, conduct investigations, analyze performance data, implement corrective actions, and collaborate with department leaders to ensure safe, high-quality patient care.
Key Responsibilities
Lead and oversee the facility's QAPI and Risk Management programs.
Maintain ongoing survey readiness and monitor compliance with CMS, Alabama Department of Public Health, and applicable regulatory requirements.
Oversee incident reporting, investigations, root cause analyses, and corrective action plans.
Conduct clinical documentation audits, quality reviews, and patient safety assessments.
Identify trends in patient safety events, clinical outcomes, and organizational performance.
Coordinate regulatory surveys, inspections, reporting, and plans of correction.
Develop and present quality and risk management reports to executive leadership.
Collaborate with Nursing, Medical Staff, Infection Prevention, Clinical Services, and other departments to improve patient outcomes.
Provide staff education and promote a culture of safety, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Ensure identified deficiencies are addressed and corrective actions are monitored for sustained effectiveness.
Qualifications
Required:
Minimum three years of progressively responsible healthcare experience, including at least two years in quality assurance, risk management, regulatory compliance, patient safety, or performance improvement.
Strong organizational, analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to conduct investigations, analyze data, and manage multiple priorities.
Knowledge of healthcare regulatory requirements, patient safety practices, and quality improvement processes.
Preferred:
Bachelor's degree in Nursing, Healthcare Administration, Public Health, or a related field.
Current RN license.
Inpatient psychiatric or behavioral health experience.
Previous leadership or program management experience.
Experience with CMS surveys, incident investigations, corrective action planning, and QAPI programs.
What We're Looking For
We are looking for someone who is not only knowledgeable about regulations but also understands how to translate those requirements into daily practice.
The successful candidate will be visible throughout the facility, proactive in identifying concerns, comfortable holding others accountable, and committed to building systems that improve patient safety and organizational performance.
Join Our Team
At The Sanctuary, our mission is to create a place where every person feels seen, respected, understood, and supported; providing compassionate mental health care that inspires hope, promotes healing, and restores purpose.
If you are passionate about behavioral health, patient safety, and making a meaningful impact through leadership, we encourage you to apply.
The Sanctuary is an equal opportunity employer.

This is a highly hands-on leadership role, with most of the VP’s time spent on the production floor understanding the operation, developing leaders, analyzing performance, and identifying opportunities for improvement. For the right person, this is a rare opportunity to make a meaningful mark on a growing business, bringing fresh ideas to the operation and helping shape how it evolves. With significant growth ahead, this leader will have the opportunity to build an operation that is stronger, more scalable, and positioned for the future.
What You'll Do
Lead day-to-day manufacturing and custom fabrication operations, driving performance across production, quality, safety, throughput, and on-time delivery.
Maintain a strong presence on the production floor, using firsthand observation and Gemba walks to understand workflow, identify constraints, and uncover opportunities for improvement.
Establish and manage production planning, scheduling, capacity, and operating rhythms that create greater visibility and accountability throughout the operation.
Apply Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, and other continuous improvement practices to improve flow, reduce waste and rework, increase throughput, and strengthen manufacturing processes.
Develop supervisors and managers through hands-on coaching, clear expectations, and accountability, strengthening both team performance and operational execution.
Evaluate opportunities to improve scalability and reduce reliance on labor through process improvements, automation, equipment, and strategic capital investment.
Partner closely with the CEO, executive leadership, and Board on operational strategy, growth initiatives, capital investments, and the infrastructure needed to support continued expansion.
What You Bring
10+ years of manufacturing operations experience, including 5+ years in senior leadership over a full plant or multiple departments.
Proven experience in custom fabrication or engineered-to-order manufacturing; metal fabrication experience is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated success using Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, or equivalent continuous improvement methods to deliver measurable operational results.
Strong command of production scheduling, capacity planning, and throughput management.
Working knowledge of manufacturing safety and quality systems.
Proven track record of coaching and developing supervisors and managers into higher levels of responsibility, while building strong relationships, maintaining accountability, and influencing teams through a constructive leadership style.
Bachelor's degree in engineering, manufacturing, business, or equivalent professional experience.
Experience in pre-engineered metal buildings, structural steel, or heavy fabrication; Lean/Six Sigma certification; ERP/Excel reporting; machine programming; or Spanish fluency are pluses.
Willingness to work fully on-site in the greater Salem area.
Our client offers a strong base plus performance-based bonus, employer-paid base-level medical coverage, voluntary dental and vision benefits, PTO, and paid holidays.
